title: Use of SkillsFuture Credit for Younger ITE Graduates to Upgrade Themselves
what_it_is: Use of SkillsFuture Credit for Younger ITE Graduates to Upgrade Themselves

sections.label: SkillsFuture Credit starting age 25
sections.summary: SkillsFuture Credit starts at 25, while under-25s use PSEAs and other subsidies and career help exist.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Education)
sentences.text: The starting age for SkillsFuture Credit is 25 years old, as it is the age where many Singaporeans would have completed their full-time education and are in, or are preparing to jointhe workforce.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Education)
sentences.text: Singaporeans under 25 years old can use their Post-Secondary Education Accounts (PSEAs) to defray out-of-pocket fees for approved programmes.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Education)
sentences.text: More importantly, beyond the SkillsFuture Credit, Singaporeans have access to a wide range of measures to support their skills development.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Education)
sentences.text: There are subsidies of up to 97% of course fees for various training programmes, such as the part-time Higher Nitec module which could cost as low as $40, after all the subsidies.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Education)
sentences.text: Institute of Technical Education (ITE) graduates who wish to enhance their employability or seek employment assistance can receive help from the ITE Career Services Centre or any of the Workforce Singapore career centres.

sections.label: ITE Work-Learn Technical Diploma
sections.summary: ITE graduates have options including the apprenticeship-based ITE Work-Learn Technical Diploma, and returning ITE graduates receive heavily subsidised support.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: The first one is, they have a range of options they can choose from to gain access to courses to support skills development and also employability.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: I will give a quick example and, that is, the recently launched ITE Work-Learn Technical Diploma.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: This is, essentially, an apprenticeship-based programme that will allow our ITE graduates to pursue a diploma even as they work.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: It is designed to enhance our ITE graduates' employability because we have structured it such that it has a very strong, on-the-job component; 70% of the curriculum is based on the on-the-job component.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: It really allows our ITE graduates not just to learn and gain industry-relevant skills, but also to gain a deep understanding of the company and also the sector.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: I want to assure the Member that even after our ITE graduates leave ITE, maybe after taking Nitec and working for a couple of years and they are still young, they want to come back and take Nitec again or Higher Nitec, they will receive the support, heavily subsidised.

sections.label: SkillsFuture Credit course directory
sections.summary: The SkillsFuture Credit directory currently has more than 18,000 modular courses, which are quite short term.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: The SkillsFuture Credit directory currently has about more than 18,000 modular	courses, and they are quite short term.
